To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

immunization of mice with soluble protein antigens, such as human growth hormone (HGH), prostatic acid phosphatas (PAP) or chorionic somatomammatropin (CS) at a dose of 115 micrograms, results in the production of hybridomas secreting antibodies against these proteins with a frequency of 0.5 to 0.8.

immunizing mice with soluble proteins, or with non-soluble antigens, using a high protein dose and a short time interval between the immunizations, results in the production of a large number of antigen-specific hybridomas.
the immunization protocol described herein allows the production of hybridomas with high SE.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of immunization protocols that allow the recovery of high frequency of specific MAbs against different types of antigens.
the development of a new immunization protocol that can be easily used in a routine immunization schedule.
the development of immunization schemes for the production of high frequency of MAbs against proteins.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
immunization with 1300 micrograms of protein is sufficient to produce high frequency (1/100) of specific hybridomas.

a high frequency of specific clones can be obtained by immunizing mice at the optimal dose of protein (1-2 mg per mouse) and by fusing spleen cells from immunized mice with myeloma cells 7-14 days after immunization.
immunization with 115-130 micrograms of protein over a period of 2 weeks is the best immunization protocol to produce a high SE of specific hybridomas against soluble proteins.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the SE is independent of the antigen used and of the immunization protocol applied.
the SE of hybridomas secreting MAbs against soluble proteins can reach values as high as those obtained for hybridomas producing MAbs against nonsoluble proteins.
the immunization protocols described here can produce high SE of positive hybridomas secreting MAbs against soluble proteins.
The main takeaway from our work is that
high frequency of antigen-specific hybridomas can be recovered by immunizing the animals with relatively small amounts of protein (1300 micrograms).
the immunization protocol described here is a very simple, inexpensive, and efficient method for generating high frequency of antigen-specific hybridomas.
high frequency of specific MAbs can be obtained in a relatively short time.
